Eukaryotic cells contain membrane-bound organelles, each with specialized functions:

| Organelle | Function |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Nucleus** | Stores genetic material (DNA) and controls cellular activities (transcription and replication). |
| **Mitochondria** | Generates chemical energy (ATP) through cellular respiration ("Powerhouse of the cell"). |
| **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)** | Rough ER synthesizes and folds proteins; Smooth ER synthesizes lipids and detoxifies chemicals. |
| **Golgi Apparatus** | Modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids for secretion or internal use. |
| **Lysosomes** | Contains digestive enzymes to break down waste materials, foreign particles, and cellular debris. |
| **Peroxisomes** | Breaks down fatty acids and detoxifies harmful metabolic byproducts like hydrogen peroxide. |
| **Chloroplasts** *(Plant cells)* | Captures light energy to produce organic molecules via photosynthesis. |
| **Vacuoles** | Storage of water, nutrients, and waste products; provides turgor pressure in plant cells. |
proTip: Keep the table concise by pairing each organelle directly with its primary biochemical role.
